title: Region-aware graceful-fallback and alert-threshold tuner
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Problem: Our oncall team is repeatedly paged during transient multi-region load spikes where throughput shifts cause short-lived token latency increases and transient 502/504 errors. Current static thresholds trigger noisy alerts and manual failovers escalate toil. Goal: implement a region-aware adaptive alert threshold tuner that reduces noisy paging, coordinates circuit-breaker sensitivity with load-shedding policies, and automates safe multi-region graceful fallback when sustained SLO degradation is detected.

Scope:
- Core service to continuously compute per-region, per-route dynamic alert thresholds from streaming telemetry (p95/p99 latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU queue depth, queue length).
- Tight integration with circuit breaker controller so the tuner adjusts sensitivity (open/half-open thresholds) based on short-term gradients and SLO burn rate.
- Automated, reversible runbook steps for safe graceful fallback (traffic steering to secondary region, scaled load-shedding, cache-only read paths) triggered when automated policy sees sustained SLO breach + CB open in primary region.
- Alerting pipeline changes: suppression windows for transient spikes, deduplication by correlated request-id, and intelligent severity escalation (page -> push -> ticket) depending on estimated customer impact.
- Console UX: per-customer opt-out, visibility of tuner decisions, and a rollback button to manually disable auto-failover.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We favor a fast-moving EWMA + gradient detector for thresholding (low compute, explainable) over a heavier ML model in the first phase. ML can be explored in a follow-up if needed.
- Conservative failover: automated fallback only after two independent signals (SLO burn rate > threshold for 3m AND circuit breaker open for 2 consecutive evaluation windows). This reduces blast radius but slightly increases mean time to automatic mitigation.
- Circuit breaker sensitivity adjustments are rate-limited and require a minimum cooldown window to avoid oscillation between regions.
- Runbook automation will be idempotent and must include human-in-the-loop confirmations for high-customer-impact customers (opt-in/out per customer).
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive thresholds deployed to staging and validated against 2 historic multi-region incidents: new thresholds should suppress >=40% of noisy pages while preserving actionable alerts
Automatic failover triggers only when both SLO burn and CB open conditions are met; verified by end-to-end test harness
Runbook automation performs safe traffic steering, applies load-shedding policy, and posts a structured incident timeline to the incident channel within 90s of trigger
Per-customer opt-out and manual rollback controls visible in Console; documentation and support playbook published
Unit tests for tuner logic + integration tests for alert pipeline and CB controller; runtime metrics and dashboard wiring in Grafana/Observability
Post-deploy 14-day evaluation shows page volume reduced by target and no increase in customer-visible errors (SLO compliance preserved)
